entry.title: TSMC's A14 is ready for design-in with PDK 0.9 (3 minute read)
entry.content:
A14 uses second-generation nanosheet transistors with flexible cell types, so designers put fast Boost Cells on critical paths and power-saving Low-Power Cells everywhere else. TSMC claims 50% better energy efficiency and 23% higher logic density than N2P, and a later move to A13 shrinks die area about 6% without changing the design flow.

entry.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million solar-powered orbital data center satellites, with 100,000 due by November 2035 (3 minute read)
entry.content:
SpaceX has been authorized to launch a constellation of up to 1 million AI satellites that would link to each other optically and reach Earth through Starlink, with the 1 million count acting as a regulatory ceiling rather than a promised fleet. SpaceX plans to equip them with Nvidia Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs, relying on Starship's falling launch costs to compete with terrestrial datacenter prices

entry.title: NERC's first standards require data centers of 50 MW or more to share power models and trip settings, after 3.8 GW of Virginia load dropped off the grid at once (4 minute read)
entry.content:
On July 22, Northern Virginia facilities drawing 3,800 MW switched to backup after a routine line fault, spiking frequency and voltage, and at least eight such events have shed 200 to 1,800 MW since 2022. AI training makes it worse, since synchronized GPUs pulse between full power and near idle, and a 100 MW facility swung 10 to 15 MW every 2.5 seconds. Simulations show those pulses can resonate with grid natural frequencies, so NERC also plans ride-through and oscillation criteria next year.

entry.title: Quick Take: AMD's Helios as a Plug-and-Play AI Appliance Standard (4 minute read)
entry.content:
AMD's Helios combines AMD CPU, GPU, and Ethernet with the ROCm framework in a plug-and-play AI solution using OCP's ORW form factor. Positioned as a competitive alternative to NVIDIA's offerings, AMD focuses on integration and easier software porting from CUDA to ROCm. Though larger cloud providers depend on NVIDIA or custom AI ASICs, smaller providers may leverage Helios's integration for straightforward deployment and operation.

entry.title: SK hynix to Start 3D DRAM Production in 2031 (2 minute read)
entry.content:

The production requires advanced techniques like multi-deck stacking and hybrid bonding, drawing from technology licensed from YMTC. This shift involves completely overhauling SK hynix's DRAM architecture and manufacturing process.

entry.title: Xpeng says its IRON humanoid will sell at roughly the median price of its EVs (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Xpeng's EVs run from 119,800 to 309,800 yuan (about $18,000 to $44,000), and an executive gave that as the benchmark for the future cost of their humanoid, IRON. IRON carries over 1,500 tactile sensing points, with 76 degrees of freedom and three in-house Turing AI chips. Mass production starts in January. Store trials follow in Q1 2027, and public sales are targeted for Q2. Xpeng wants to sell tens of thousands next year, funded by a $900 million robotics round at a $6.3 billion valuation, while its stock is down 55% this year.

entry.title: Insect-size flying robots could leave the lab within two years, but onboard power, sensing, and control are the bottleneck (4 minute read)
entry.content:
University of Washington's Sawyer Fuller predicts a fully autonomous insect-size flyer could fly free soon, though techniques from larger drones break down at this scale and onboard controllers and sensors add weight. MIT's wing-halved design hovered for about 1,000 seconds, 100 times longer than prior bots, and leaves room for batteries and sensors. Other designs, like FVW-Fly, control altitude but still lack directional control.

entry.title: Bambu Lab's P3C brings a seven-tool changer to a $1,149 printer, about half the price of the H3C (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Instead of purging one nozzle on every color change, the Swaptek system swaps between separate nozzles in about six seconds, with five 0.4 mm tools included and two open slots that cost $99 each to fill. The build volume is 256 x 256 x 260 mm versus 330 x 320 x 325 mm on the H3C, and the bundled AMS 3P loads filament manually, which is the main compromise. It went on sale on November 24, with the seven-tool kit at $1,299.

entry.title: LLMs handle Verilog but not layouts or waveforms, and agents multiply load on design data systems by 10 to 20x (14 minute read)
entry.content:

Each engineer directing 10 to 20 agents scales version control, NFS, and license demand the same way, and IP governance is a worry. Customers are drifting back from air-gapped open models toward frontier ones, while hybrid specialized models may handle things like temporal assertions.

entry.title: Boom Supersonic lights its in-house engine core for the first time, a six-stage compressor and single-stage turbine shared by a data center turbine and Overture's engine (2 minute read)
entry.content:
The core reached 6,500 rpm with nearly 2,000 sensors on its second light-off attempt, on a Colorado rig that uses a vacuum pump to simulate the bypass duct and a variable nozzle to simulate the low-pressure turbine. The same core underpins the 42 MW Superpower gas turbine for AI data centers and the 40,000 lb Symphony turbofan for the Mach 1.7 Overture, with over 75% commonality. Boom is also building a tooling-free foundry for single-crystal turbine blades.

entry.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15 with a vision encoder shared across FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, claiming 25x better critical intervention rate (3 minute read)
entry.content:

A new Reality View replaces separate model signals with one end-to-end visualization that uses less compute. v15 also targets known weak spots, including sign reading, potholes, standing water, school zones, and speed cameras, but Tesla published only the 25x multiplier, not the underlying intervention rate. It also loosens driver monitoring at higher-speed profiles.

entry.title: A one-crystal-thick film of mixed nanocrystals can boost or block infrared light, and a new model shows how to tune it (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Researchers mixed two kinds of tiny crystals, differing in how much tin they contain, into a film just one crystal thick. When infrared light hits it, each crystal's electrons ripple at a slightly different rate, and those ripples overlap in the tiny gaps between neighbors. The film is made in solution, so it avoids expensive etching, and it could be used in thermal camouflage or self-cooling surfaces.

entry.title: Google's quantum processor wins a contextuality game 98.3% of the time against an 88.9% classical limit, across tasks up to 105 qubits (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Contextuality means a qubit's measured value depends on which compatible measurements are made alongside it. New research shows it survives at scale instead of only in few-particle systems. The same game doubles as a sensitive test for subtle hardware errors, which helps validate processors for chemistry and materials science. The qubits also beat constrained classical strategies on tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.

entry.title: Silicon photonics is the next step for AI data centers (3 minute read)
entry.content:
With construction spending above a $75 billion annual pace and about 3,000 buildings planned or underway, phase-one architecture choices will carry into capacity arriving at the end of the decade. The interconnect between chips sets power per token, and moving data as infrared light through silicon waveguides removes the reach limit. Photonics-SOI, PD-SOI, and RF-SOI platforms each optimize for different metrics and aren't interchangeable.

On Jalapeño, the matrix and SIMD blocks shrank 10% to 13%, confirmed in silicon, partly by rewriting adders and multipliers, including a multiplier cut from two cycles to one. The thrust structure, housing all 13 Aeon R engines, fluid lines, and avionics, is being mated to stage one. At LC-16, the launch table framing is done and a second pad lift cylinder has arrived. entry.title: Detachable fiber connectors are emerging for CPO and NPO because standard fibers can't be reworked, tray-handled, or tested at volume (15 minute read)
entry.content:
Fibers bonded to photonic chips can't be reworked if one breaks, dangle during pick-and-place, and eat die-edge shoreline, since 125 µm cladding adds up across 16 fibers. Designs now bring light out at the edge or through a 45° mirror, with lenses, snap-fit alignment, or magnets replacing active alignment. Senko and Advantest demonstrated a test connector surviving 10,000 matings with little loss variation, but there's still no standard interface.

entry.title: SHAPE trains a VLA on egocentric human video with discrete action tokens and two parallel action streams for a bimanual robot with 22-DoF hands (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Human video only gives retargeted end-effector actions, not the joint commands robots need. SHAPE's Qwen3-VL-4B backbone predicts discrete EEF action tokens as an auxiliary task, while a shared flow-matching expert outputs separate EEF and joint streams. Joint readout scores 0.80 across six tasks versus 0.63 for π0.5, and EEF readout via IK transfers better from humans. After human-data pretraining, it learns new tasks from human demos with no task-specific robot data.

entry.title: A 3D-printed, electronics-free soft hexapod hits 4.72 m/s by reusing compressed air like a compound steam engine (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Higher air pressure speeds up a pneumatic robot but wastes energy, so the team routes air through small high-pressure chambers that power the valves, then through larger low-pressure chambers that move the legs, as in a compound steam engine. The six-legged robot is printed in one piece from one soft material and runs about 100 times faster than the 2022 version, over sand, mulch, and concrete, and in water. It's still tethered to an air compressor.

entry.title: Backplane is an alpha, open-source KiCad fork where AI agents design boards through KiCad's IPC and CLI (1 minute read)
entry.content:
Agents drive KiCad directly through kicad_ipc and kicad-cli instead of rewriting files, so every board stays human-editable. Persistent bots run in threads with memory, routines, and webhooks. The built-in KiStack adds 11 auto-updating skills for schematics, placement, layout, panelization, BOMs, and fab outputs, with the export skill running ERC and DRC and generating gerbers, drill, pick-and-place, STEP, and renders. The demo is an STM32N657 SoM, and it ships with a 199-footprint library.

It's rated 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuous at 34.5 kV with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA peak, made in the US, operating in 2027. That's about 50% more than the 5 MW Heron Link from ex-Tesla exec Drew Baglino's startup, which claims 98.6% efficiency, a Morgan Hill factory, and customers like Vantage and Intersect. Tesla hasn't shared efficiency or pricing.

entry.title: A 125-qubit chip teleports an error-corrected qubit using weaker entanglement than expected (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Teleporting a protected qubit between quantum processors needs a good-enough entanglement link, and below a certain quality it fails. By balancing the two kinds of errors in the code, researchers made their 125-qubit chip tolerate a much weaker link, raising the threshold from 0.122π to 0.175π. Theory suggests even very weak entanglement could eventually work, which would make linking error-corrected quantum computers easier.

entry.title: Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical links (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Marvell's module, from its $3.5B Celestial AI acquisition, stacks 72 GB of HBM3e and eight DDR5 channels on a silicon photonic interposer with 900 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth. Penguin's box holds 16 modules behind a 57.6 Tbps optical shuffle, serving up to 16 servers over NICs or CPO and NPO optics, bypassing CXL for the optical modes. An HBM cache-through mode gives HBM speed with DDR5 capacity, aimed at KV cache offload, with systems due in the second half of next year.
